summary.headline: Kilburn Q2 FY27 consol revenue flat YoY at INR153.1 crore; standalone revenue fell 39% to INR69.5 crore, subsidiaries carried the group.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue was INR153.1 crore, roughly flat YoY and up 30.9% QoQ, while H1 consolidated revenue fell 4.5% to INR270.1 crore. Consolidated PAT was INR16.5 crore for Q2 and INR29.6 crore for H1. Standalone Q2 revenue dropped to INR69.5 crore from INR114.8 crore, with PAT at INR5.7 crore versus INR18 crore, which management attributed to customers delaying decisions amid geopolitical uncertainty. Subsidiaries (ME Energy, Monga Strayfield) roughly doubled H1 revenue to INR141.7 crore and now exceed half of group revenue. Management cut the FY27 group revenue indication to INR600-650 crore from an earlier INR700 crore standalone view and described FY27 as a transition year.

segments.name: Kilburn Engineering (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR69.5 crore vs INR114.8 crore YoY; PAT INR5.7 crore vs INR18 crore. Management says decline is timing (customer deferrals in export and capital goods), not loss of competitiveness. Capacity at Ambernath and Saravali could reach INR750-800 crore on strong order book, per management.

segments.name: ME Energy (subsidiary, waste heat recovery / process equipment)
segments.commentary: Entered ferro-alloy space via a Bhutan order and qualified for a cement-plant waste heat recovery boiler bid. Phase 2 Pune expansion (2 bays added) being commissioned, expected complete by March; theoretical capacity upwards of INR300 crore, with management citing INR350-400 crore post-expansion.

segments.name: Monga Strayfield (subsidiary, RF dryers and precision engineering)
segments.commentary: Enclosures for data centres, transformers and battery storage. INR25 crore capex approved, 6-9 months to implement, capacity addition from January. Revenue indicated at INR50-60 crore in FY27 on current capacity; Vertiv indicated INR90 crore requirement this year; company revenue potential over INR200 crore from INR100 crore base.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue indicated at INR600-650 crore; management says it could shift, especially in Q4, and is not giving formal current-year guidance.
Management expects to maintain last year's overall top line by H2, with growth shifting toward subsidiaries.
EBITDA margin: long-term average of around 20% on a blended group basis; no quarterly or half-yearly margin guidance.
Medium-term: 20-25% CAGR from FY26 base (about INR620 crore) to FY28, implying INR900-1,000 crore revenue at 20% EBITDA margin.
Order intake target of INR800 crore for FY27 (INR300+ crore booked till date), with closing order book expected to be higher than INR471 crore.
Group manufacturing infrastructure targeted at more than INR1,000 crore annual revenue capacity within a couple of years; INR25 crore data-centre capex to be completed in 6-9 months.
Expects cash flow from operations to remain negative in FY27, with the negative figure reducing.
capex_capacity: Kilburn Saravali expansion and ME Energy Phase 2 Pune expansion underway, expected complete by Q3 / early Q4 FY27; ME Energy commissioning to finish by March.

Monga Strayfield Pune plant expansion: INR25 crore Board-approved investment for enclosures, cabinets and engineered assemblies; 6-9 months to implement; capacity starts kicking in January, full capacity in first half of FY28.
Kilburn standalone capex of about INR25 crore earmarked for the current and previous quarter, to be commissioned by December; management said nothing additional planned for now.

Monga Strayfield revenue potential scaling to over INR200 crore from INR100 crore base (including RF dryers); ME Energy and Monga together can deliver over INR500 crore revenue in FY28, subject to orders.
demand_pricing: Q2 order inflow INR136 crore across fertilizers, carbon black and AI data centres; largest order book segments are fertilizers, carbon black, iron and steel and nuclear power.

Management says INR200-250 crore of opportunities are near closure (Middle East, Far East, one domestic nuclear, plus one more) expected within 45-60 days; a Middle East order is tied to a JV formed last week.
Some orders deferred by a couple of quarters; a carbon black order was deferred by a customer.
Enclosure demand exceeds supply: company says it is supplying at full capacity to existing customers; Vertiv is the main anchor customer.
Pricing: management says it typically has no price escalation clauses; it protects margins by procuring key raw materials immediately on order award.
Receivables: some over 120 days and some over 180 days, linked to customer commissioning milestones; management did not give a percentage.

qa_highlights.question: What are data-centre enclosures, who are the listed competitors, and does precision engineering include defence or aerospace?
qa_highlights.answer: Monga's enclosures are customised sheet-metal cabinets for housing servers, batteries and networking/power hardware; work is limited to power transformer and data-centre sectors, with no aerospace or defence work. Competitors are large global players sourcing from qualified vendor pools; no certifications are pending from foreign customers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR800 crore order-book target for FY27 realistic versus the INR471 crore current order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified INR800 crore is order intake for the year, not closing order book; over INR300 crore booked to date. Closing order book is expected to be higher than today's INR471 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the standalone top line and EBITDA outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Group revenue indication INR600-650 crore, with earlier INR700 crore view for standalone now superseded; no quarterly margin guidance. Long-term EBITDA margin around 20%; management declined to guide to a specific H2 margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is current utilisation and when will data-centre capacity ramp up?
qa_highlights.answer: Kilburn Ambernath and Saravali could reach INR750-800 crore; Monga capacity addition starts January, ME Energy bays being commissioned by March. Data-centre revenue expected to rise over next 4-8 quarters as capacity is added.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall in Q2 and what should be expected in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin fall attributed to product mix, higher employee cost, and higher raw material value as a share of order value rather than raw material price escalation. Management reiterated 20% aim but declined to predict quarterly margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is ME Energy's expansion capacity and revenue potential beyond FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said post-expansion ME Energy can go beyond INR350-400 crore with EPC orders; capacity is not the binding constraint, and execution capability is.

risks_watch: Standalone order conversion: the INR200-250 crore pipeline must close in 45-60 days to support H2 and FY28 growth; deferrals have already occurred.
Margin pressure: Q2 EBITDA margin about 16.5% vs 20% target; management declined to commit to quarterly margins and said it may miss by 1-2%.
Full-year revenue slippage: FY27 indication cut to INR600-650 crore; a Q4 dependency on order timing.
Data-centre ramp execution: INR25 crore capex timeline of 6-9 months; INR100-120 crore revenue ambition depends on Vertiv and other customer orders not yet secured.
Working capital: cash flow from operations negative; receivables over 180 days in some cases.
Promoter pledge of about 5 lakh shares (under 1% of promoter holding) created in Sep/Oct for corporate requirements at an entity, with no timeline for release given.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the group model and FY28 CAGR target, but defensive and evasive on quarterly and H2 margins and on FY27 standalone revenue, repeatedly declining to give quarter-specific guidance. Management attributes weakness to timing of customer decisions and expresses urgency around orders expected in the next 45-60 days.
key_quotes: Our consol order book stood at INR471 crores as on 30th September, broadly in line with INR485 crores at the start of the quarter, even after executing INR151 crores during the quarter.
The decline came from slower decision-making by customers and not from loss of any competitiveness.
We are sitting on more than INR250 crores of opportunities, which we are about to close any time.
Whether it is going to be 18%, 19%, 20% or 21%, it's not possible for us to predict and guide you.
